SeriesLinearAlgAccessor::lu_solve¶

Back to SeriesLinearAlgAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

Series SeriesLinearAlgAccessor::lu_solve(const Series& b) const
Series SeriesLinearAlgProxy::lu_solve() const

What It Does¶

Solves A X = B for a general nonsingular square coefficient matrix A, which is the Series owning the accessor. Despite the method’s name, callers pass the original coefficient matrix; factorization and pivoting happen inside the operation. Do not pass a packed LU factor.

General Systems Through Elimination¶

LU elimination decomposes a general square system into triangular stages while pivoting protects against unsuitable diagonal choices. It handles matrices that need not be symmetric or positive definite. When stronger structure is known, a Cholesky or triangular solve can avoid unnecessary work.

Parameter And Shapes¶

b may be [...,n] or [...,n,k]. Vector right-hand sides return [...,n,1]; matrix right-hand sides preserve [...,n,k]. Leading dimensions of A and b broadcast, while A must end in [n,n].

Gradient¶

For X=A^-1 B and incoming G, reverse mode uses dB=A^-T G and dA=-(A^-T G)X^T. Broadcasted batch sensitivities reduce back to each original operand shape.

Examples¶

Example 1. Solve one right-hand side.

auto a = pluss::make_series({{3.0, 1.0}, {1.0, 2.0}});
std::cout << a.linearalg.lu_solve(pluss::make_series({9.0, 8.0})) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,1], strides=[1,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[[2],
  [3]]

Example 2. Columns of a matrix right-hand side are solved together.

auto a = pluss::make_series({{3.0, 1.0}, {1.0, 2.0}});
auto b = pluss::make_series({{9.0, 1.0}, {8.0, 0.0}});
std::cout << a.linearalg.lu_solve(b) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[2, 0.4],
  [3, -0.2]]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The owner is the original coefficient matrix, not a precomputed LU object.

  • Singular matrices fail because the solution is not unique.

  • A very ill-conditioned matrix may produce a large residual even when formally nonsingular.

  • Prefer solving to explicitly multiplying by inverse().

Summary¶

lu_solve() solves general square systems, supports multiple and broadcasted right-hand sides, and differentiates with respect to both coefficients and data.

See Also¶

  • cholesky_solve: SPD systems from a reusable factor.

  • triangular_solve: systems already in triangular form.
